annotation_description: GLM47 Gramps has an excellent opening hand with Sol Ring and Silver Myr, which gives explosive turn 1 development. Going first maximizes this tempo advantage, as they could play Plains → Sol Ring → Silver Myr before anyone else has done anything. By choosing an opponent to go first, they lose the tempo advantage of their premium opening hand.

Playing a basic Island on turn 1 when Terramorphic Expanse is available. Terramorphic Expanse should be played first since it enters tapped and can fetch any basic land, providing color flexibility later. Playing it turn 1 minimizes the tempo loss of it entering tapped. The player's hand has Howling Mine (2 mana, colorless) as the earliest play, so turn 2 they want untapped mana. Playing Terramorphic Expanse now and cracking it end of turn for a Plains or Island gives them an untapped basic on turn 2, same as playing a basic now. But it preserves flexibility - they can decide which color they need based on what they draw. Additionally, Myriad Landscape also enters tapped and could be considered for turn 1, but Terramorphic Expanse is better turn 1 since it can be cracked immediately to thin the deck and provide the needed color.

With Sol Ring and Plains available (3 mana), the player chose to cast Abzan Falconer (2/3 with outlast and flying-granting) over Ainok Bond-Kin (2/1 with outlast and first-strike-granting). While Abzan Falconer is a fine card, the player missed the opportunity to play Ainok Bond-Kin for {1}{W} and also play the Forest from hand on the same turn. By casting Abzan Falconer (which costs {2}{W}, using all 3 mana), they could still play the Forest but it doesn't matter since all mana is spent. However, the real issue is sequencing: they should have played Forest first before casting any spell. Looking at the choices offered (Ainok Bond-Kin, Forest, Abzan Falconer), playing Forest first is strictly better sequencing since it gives access to 4 mana total (Plains, Forest, Sol Ring = {W}{G}{C}{C}), which doesn't change what can be cast this turn but is good practice. More importantly, with 4 mana after playing Forest, they could cast Ainok Bond-Kin ({1}{W}) and still have {G}{C} left over - though nothing else costs that. Alternatively, Abzan Falconer at {2}{W} uses 3 of 4 mana. The Falconer is arguably the better card (2/3 vs 2/1, flying vs first strike), so the creature choice is reasonable. But they should have played Forest first before casting the spell - casting spells before playing lands is a sequencing error.

Johnny played Forest instead of Contested Cliffs as their land for the turn. Contested Cliffs is a land that taps for colorless mana but also has the activated ability to make a Beast creature fight an opponent's creature. Given that Johnny's deck contains Beast creatures (Ravenous Baloth, Marath, and the Beast token from One Dozen Eyes), getting Contested Cliffs into play early provides a repeatable removal engine. Playing Forest here is slightly worse since Johnny already has a Selesnya Guildgate for green mana and Sol Ring for colorless. The Contested Cliffs only produces colorless like Sol Ring already does, but its fight ability is a unique and powerful effect worth establishing early. However, Johnny does need colored mana for expensive spells like Warstorm Surge (5R) and One Dozen Eyes (5G), so a basic Forest has some merit for mana development.

Playing Myriad Landscape (which enters tapped) on turn 2 when the player has Howling Mine (2 mana) in hand and only 1 untapped land means they cannot cast Howling Mine this turn. If they had played Plains or Mountain instead (which enter untapped), they would have had 2 mana available to cast Howling Mine on turn 2, getting the card draw engine online earlier. Terramorphic Expanse would also have been better as it fixes colors and thins the deck while still providing a land that can be cracked at end of turn. Myriad Landscape enters tapped AND costs 2 + tap + sacrifice to activate later, so playing it this early when you need colored mana and have a 2-drop to cast is suboptimal.

With 4 lands (Plains, Forest, Sol Ring, and now Blighted Woodland) plus Sol Ring, Coach has 5 mana available this turn (Plains + Forest + Sol Ring for 4, but Blighted Woodland enters untapped so that's 5 total). Growth Spasm costs 3 mana (2G) and would ramp by fetching a basic land + creating an Eldrazi Spawn token (which can sac for colorless). Playing Blighted Woodland first is fine as a land drop, but the question is whether to cast Growth Spasm this turn instead of just playing the land. With Blighted Woodland in play, Coach has Plains, Forest, Sol Ring, Blighted Woodland = 5 mana. Growth Spasm costs 2G, leaving 2 mana open. This would accelerate toward Citadel Siege (costs 2WW) next turn. Actually, playing Blighted Woodland and then casting Growth Spasm would be the optimal line - play land, then cast the ramp spell. But the decision here is just about the land drop, which is correct. However, looking more carefully: Coach could have cast Growth Spasm (using Forest + Sol Ring for 2G = 3 mana) and THEN played Blighted Woodland as the land drop. But Growth Spasm is a sorcery that searches for a basic land - playing Blighted Woodland first doesn't change available mana since it also taps for colorless. Wait - the decision shows Coach chose Blighted Woodland as their play. The question is whether they should have cast Growth Spasm instead or in addition. With Plains + Forest + Sol Ring = 4 mana, they can cast Growth Spasm (2G) using Forest + Sol Ring (1 colorless + 1 colorless + 1 green = 3 mana), then play Blighted Woodland. That would give them 6+ mana sources next turn (Plains, Forest, Sol Ring, Blighted Woodland, fetched basic, Eldrazi Spawn), enabling Citadel Siege. If they just play Blighted Woodland, they have 5 mana next turn - not enough for Citadel Siege (2WW needs 4 mana including 2 white, and they only have 1 Plains). Actually with Growth Spasm they could fetch a Plains, giving them 2 white sources. This seems like a clear case where casting Growth Spasm + playing Blighted Woodland would have been better than just playing the land.

In a multiplayer game at 40 life, declining free attacks is debatable. KimiK2 Valley and Qwen3L Johnny have no creatures to block, so Abzan Falconer could attack for 2 damage completely risk-free. While multiplayer politics can justify not attacking early, passing on free damage with no downside is at least worth questioning.

GLM47 cast Thoughtcast before playing a land. They have Port Town in hand and could reveal Plains or Island to have it enter untapped. Playing Port Town first would give them an additional artifact-independent mana source and wouldn't cost anything. More importantly, they should play a land before casting spells as a general sequencing principle - there's no reason to cast Thoughtcast first since they have enough mana already (Sol Ring + Silver Myr + Island = 4 mana, Thoughtcast with 2 artifacts costs 3). However, playing a land first preserves more options after seeing the two drawn cards.

Player miscalculated their available mana, thinking Contested Cliffs produces {W} or {R} (it produces {C}) and apparently forgetting Selesnya Guildgate can produce {G}. Actual available mana was {G}{G}{C}{C}{C} (5 total), which is enough for both Ravenous Baloth ({2}{G}{G}) and Drumhunter ({3}{G}). The player's reasoning concluded they couldn't cast either spell, potentially leading to a suboptimal choice or delayed development.

KimiK2 Valley cast Howling Mine before playing a land for the turn. They have Plains, Terramorphic Expanse, Transguild Promenade, and Mountain in hand. Playing a land first (like Plains or Terramorphic Expanse) would preserve the option to cast Howling Mine with different mana if needed, and ensures they don't accidentally miss their land drop. More importantly, they should have played Terramorphic Expanse and cracked it to fix mana for Gwafa Hazid (which needs W and U), or played Plains to have 3 mana available. The sequencing of casting spells before playing lands is a basic mistake, though here Howling Mine only costs 2 so the Island + Myriad Landscape cover it. The real concern is that Howling Mine in a 4-player game gives 3 opponents extra cards while only giving you 1 extra card - a net disadvantage. However, this is a group hug style deck so it may be intentional. The land-before-spell sequencing is still a minor error.

Playing Transguild Promenade when you have no untapped lands to pay the {1} entry cost means you must sacrifice it immediately, wasting your land drop for the turn. With Terramorphic Expanse, Plains, and Mountain all available as alternative land drops, any of those would have been strictly better. Terramorphic Expanse would let you fetch a basic land (fixing colors), Plains gives immediate white mana, and Mountain gives red mana - all without the downside of losing the land.

Casting Citadel Siege on turn 4 is a strong play for the +1/+1 counter strategy with Abzan Falconer (grants flying) and Ainok Bond-Kin (grants first strike). However, Bastion Protector costs only 3 mana and would immediately provide a 3/3 body on board, which is relevant for board presence in the early game. Citadel Siege won't provide value until the next combat step. More importantly, the player could have considered playing Bastion Protector first and saving Citadel Siege for next turn when they'd have more mana available anyway. That said, Citadel Siege choosing Khans synergizes extremely well with the outlast creatures already on board, giving them counters without spending mana on outlast (which requires tapping the creature). This is a reasonable play, but the question is whether deploying a 3/3 body now (Bastion Protector) and Citadel Siege next turn would have been better sequencing, since Bastion Protector could also be a target for the Citadel Siege counters next turn.

Attacking with a 0/1 Eldrazi Spawn token deals 0 damage and accomplishes nothing. The token is more valuable as a mana source (sacrifice for {C}) or as a chump blocker. Sending it into combat risks losing it to any blocker while dealing no damage.

Playing Boros Garrison before casting a creature is slightly suboptimal but not terrible. Boros Garrison enters tapped and requires bouncing a land, which means the player loses mana availability this turn. With 4 mana available (Selesnya Guildgate, Sol Ring, Forest, Contested Cliffs), they could cast Drumhunter (3G) or Ravenous Baloth (2GG) first, then play Boros Garrison next turn. By playing Garrison now, they bounce a land and end up with all tapped lands, unable to cast anything meaningful this turn. However, Garrison does fix red mana for future turns and the player may be planning ahead. The Howling Mine trigger means they'll draw extra cards, so developing mana isn't unreasonable.

Bouncing Boros Garrison to hand means it must be replayed next turn and will enter tapped again, costing a full turn of mana development. Boros Garrison produces 2 mana (RW) when untapped. By returning it, Johnny loses access to that mana this turn cycle and next turn must replay it tapped again, effectively wasting two land drops on the same land. Returning Selesnya Guildgate (which only produces G or W, a subset of what Boros Garrison provides) or Contested Cliffs (which requires RG to activate and has limited utility early) would have been better. Returning a basic Forest would keep the bounce land in play producing 2 mana, though Forest is untapped. The best return is likely Selesnya Guildgate since Boros Garrison already produces both colors Guildgate would, and Guildgate entered tapped previously anyway.

message: Pick triggered ability (goes to the stack first)
annotation_description: Putting the +1/+1 counter on Leinore instead of Ainok Bond-Kin misses out on activating Ainok Bond-Kin's first strike granting ability. Both targets enable coven (three distinct powers), but Ainok Bond-Kin with a counter would grant first strike to all creatures with +1/+1 counters, which is meaningful with Abzan Falconer also on board (future counters grant both flying and first strike).

Attacking with the Eldrazi Spawn Token (0/1) deals 0 damage and risks losing it if blocked, though GLM47 Gramps has Katsumasa (3/3 flying) which can't block a ground creature, and Silver Myr is tapped. The token has value as a sacrifice for {C} mana, which could be relevant for future plays. However, the attack deals 0 damage anyway since it's a 0/1, so it accomplishes nothing even if unblocked. The token's sacrifice ability for colorless mana could be more useful kept in reserve.

Katsumasa's upkeep trigger allows putting +1/+1 counters on up to three noncreature artifacts for free. GLM47 controls Sol Ring which is a noncreature artifact. Putting counters on it has no downside and makes it stronger when later animated by Katsumasa's activated ability.

message: Select card to discard (selected 1 of 2, min 2)
annotation_description: GLM47 is discarding to hand size and chose to discard Surgehacker Mech, a powerful 5/5 menace Vehicle that deals damage on entry based on Vehicles controlled — which synergizes perfectly with Katsumasa, the Animator (who can animate artifacts and put +1/+1 counters on them). Katsumasa is already on the battlefield, making Surgehacker Mech a high-value card. Meanwhile, GLM47 has 3 Plains and 2 Islands in hand — they only need 1-2 more lands and could safely discard excess basic lands instead.

Boros Garrison enters tapped and requires bouncing a land. By bouncing itself, the player essentially wasted their entire land drop for the turn — they end up with the same number of lands in play as before (the Garrison replaces itself but is tapped), and they have to replay it next turn, losing another land drop to the bounce. This creates a two-turn tempo loss for no gain.

Playing Forest instead of Terramorphic Expanse is slightly suboptimal. Terramorphic Expanse should be played first because it enters untapped and can be cracked immediately (or later) to fetch any basic land needed, providing flexibility. Playing a basic Forest locks in the land choice now, whereas Terramorphic Expanse keeps options open and also thins the deck. Additionally, the player has Kynaios and Tiro of Meletis as their commander (RGWU), and Terramorphic Expanse could fetch whatever color is most needed at the time it's cracked. Playing the Forest from hand means the Terramorphic Expanse will be played on a later turn, delaying its utility by a turn.

Akroan Horse is a 4-mana card that gives an opponent a 0/4 defender while giving you 1/1 tokens each upkeep - it's not great but it's not the worst discard. However, discarding Mountain seems strictly better here. Valley already has an Island and Forest on the battlefield plus Myriad Landscape, and has a Plains and Terramorphic Expanse in hand. The Mountain is the least useful card since Valley's colored mana needs (for cards like Gwafa Hazid which needs W/U, Windborn Muse which needs W, Humble Defector which needs R) can mostly be met by existing lands and the Terramorphic Expanse. Meanwhile, Akroan Horse at least has some utility as a token generator in multiplayer, and with Howling Mine drawing extra cards, Valley may want to deploy it eventually.

Attacking with all creatures (including Abzan Falconer and Ainok Bond-Kin) is questionable. These are key outlast creatures that form the backbone of Coach's +1/+1 counter strategy. Without any counters on them yet, they're just small bodies (2/3 and 2/1) that could easily be blocked and killed. The Eldrazi Spawn Token (0/1) also can't deal damage. Attacking into GLM47 Gramps who has Katsumasa (3/3 flyer) and Silver Myr available as blockers risks losing important synergy pieces for minimal damage. The Ainok Bond-Kin at 2/1 is particularly vulnerable. Coach should be developing their board and using outlast to build up counters rather than making ineffective attacks.

message: Select card to discard (selected 0 of 2, min 2)
annotation_description: GLM47 Gramps is discarding to hand size and chose to discard Exotic Orchard and an Island. Exotic Orchard is a versatile mana-fixing land that can produce any color an opponent's land could produce, which is especially valuable in a multiplayer game where opponents have diverse land bases. With only 4 lands in play (Island, Sol Ring, Silver Myr, Port Town) and Hanna, Ship's Navigator in hand (which costs 1WU), color fixing is important. Exotic Orchard would help cast multicolored spells and provide flexibility. Discarding two basic Islands instead would preserve the more valuable land while still reducing hand size.

message: Select card to discard (selected 0 of 2, min 2)
annotation_description: Johnny is forced to discard 2 cards (likely down to hand size of 7). They chose to discard Mountain and Khalni Garden. However, Khalni Garden is a land that creates a 0/1 Plant token when it enters - it has real utility beyond just being a land. Meanwhile, Boros Guildgate is a strictly worse land option (enters tapped, only produces R or W which Boros Garrison already covers better). Discarding Boros Guildgate instead of Khalni Garden would have preserved a land that provides both mana fixing AND a free creature token, which synergizes with Warstorm Surge and Rampaging Baloths (landfall triggers). The Mountain discard is reasonable since they already have color sources, but Khalni Garden over Boros Guildgate is a value loss.

Playing Gruul Turf enters tapped and bounces a land, leaving only Island + Forest (2 mana) available this turn. Playing Plains instead would give 3 untapped mana (Island + Forest + Plains), enabling an immediate cast of Gwafa Hazid, Profiteer (1WU) - a strong tempo play that could start neutralizing threats. The Gruul Turf can be played next turn after establishing board presence.

Bouncing Gruul Turf back to hand instead of a basic land means KimiK2 Valley loses a net land on the battlefield. Gruul Turf taps for RG (two mana), so bouncing it means replaying it next turn (entering tapped again) and losing tempo. By contrast, bouncing a basic land like Island or Forest would leave Gruul Turf on the battlefield producing RG, while the basic land could simply be replayed next turn untapped. The player ends up in a loop of replaying Gruul Turf repeatedly without net mana advancement. With a hand containing multiple lands to play (Plains, Terramorphic Expanse, Mountain) and expensive spells to cast (Windborn Muse at 4, Rubblehulk at 6, Reverse the Sands at 8), falling behind on mana development is costly.

message: Select card to discard (selected 0 of 2, min 2)
annotation_description: Discarded Rubblehulk instead of Reverse the Sands. Rubblehulk has a flexible Bloodrush ability ({1}{R}{G} to give an attacking creature +X/+X where X = lands controlled), making it useful even without casting it for 6 mana. Reverse the Sands costs 8 mana and is highly situational - currently all players are at 40 life except one at 21.

message: Select card to discard (selected 1 of 2, min 2)
annotation_description: With only 4 lands in play and needing to develop mana, discarding a basic Mountain (a land drop) over Reverse the Sands (an 8-mana situational spell they won't cast for many turns while at 40 life) is debatable. Extra land drops are valuable when behind on mana development.

Shamanic Revelation draws cards equal to the number of creatures you control. Gem3F Coach controls only 3 creatures (Abzan Falconer, Ainok Bond-Kin, Eldrazi Spawn Token), so this draws only 3 cards for 5 mana with no Ferocious triggers (no creature has power 4+). More importantly, casting this 5-mana sorcery before playing the Forest from hand means less mana available this turn and potentially next turn. Additionally, casting Bastion Protector (3 mana) or Eternal Witness (3 mana, returning Growth Spasm for ramp) would develop the board more efficiently. Playing the Forest first, then casting Talisman of Unity (2 mana) would set up better future turns. The Shamanic Revelation for 3 cards isn't terrible, but the sequencing is wrong — the Forest should be played first, and there may be better uses of 5 mana when you only draw 3 cards and have no board development.

Cast Bastion Protector without a commander on the battlefield, making it just a vanilla 3/3. Meanwhile, the hand is loaded with expensive cards (Sigarda 5 mana, Cleansing Nova 5, Dearly Departed 6, Somberwald Beastmaster 7) that desperately need mana acceleration.

GLM47 declined to interact with a 10/10 Herald of War and a 4/3 Ainok Bond-Kin attacking them for 14 damage total, dropping from 21 to 7 life. Herald of War is an escalating threat that grows every attack and was already enormous. At 7 life, GLM47 is in critical danger of dying to almost any subsequent attack.
GLM47 Gramps is at 2 life and chose not to block what appears to be an incoming attack (likely Abzan Falconer, a 2/3). Taking 2 damage at 2 life is lethal.

GLM47 Gramps is at 2 life and chose to put all three +1/+1 counters on Sol Ring, which is their own artifact. Katsumasa's upkeep trigger lets you put counters on up to three target noncreature artifacts - these could be different artifacts. The player could have targeted opponent artifacts like Howling Mine (which is actively hurting them by giving opponents extra cards while they're at 2 life) or other opponent artifacts. More importantly, they're putting all 3 counters on Sol Ring when they could spread them across different artifacts. However, the biggest issue is that Sol Ring is already their own artifact and they only seem to have Sol Ring and Silver Myr as artifacts (Silver Myr is a creature so it doesn't qualify as noncreature). They chose Sol Ring three times, putting 3 counters on it. But Katsumasa can animate noncreature artifacts into creatures - so buffing Sol Ring to later animate it as a bigger creature is a reasonable plan. Still, at 2 life, the Howling Mine giving all opponents extra draws is extremely dangerous. They should have targeted the opponent's Howling Mine with at least one counter to set up animating it or simply to have the option. Actually, looking more carefully - the choices offered were 'Abzan Falconer, Talisman of Unity, Sol Ring' which are the noncreature artifacts available. Abzan Falconer is a creature belonging to Gem3F Coach, Talisman of Unity isn't on anyone's board that I can see. Wait - the choices presented seem limited. The selected 2 of 3 message and the fact they chose Sol Ring suggests they already selected some targets. The final result shows all counters on Sol Ring. Given they're at 2 life, putting counters on Sol Ring to animate it as a blocker is reasonable, but putting all 3 on the same artifact rather than spreading them is suboptimal if other valid targets existed.

message: Select card to discard (selected 0 of 2, min 2)
annotation_description: Discarding Command Tower is a significant mistake. Command Tower is one of the best lands in Commander, entering untapped and producing any color in your commander's color identity (RGW for Marath). Johnny needs to discard 2 cards from a hand of 9, and has Boros Guildgate (enters tapped, produces only R or W) and Boros Garrison (enters tapped, bounces a land) as clearly inferior land options. War Cadence is also a low-impact card in this board state. Discarding Command Tower over these weaker options loses significant mana fixing and tempo in future turns.

Playing Plains instead of Terramorphic Expanse is slightly suboptimal. Terramorphic Expanse can be cracked to fetch any basic land (including a Plains if needed), providing more flexibility for future turns and thinning the deck. Additionally, with Gruul Turf available, playing Terramorphic Expanse now (crack it for a basic) and then playing Gruul Turf next turn to bounce and replay a land would maximize mana development. The Plains is a fine play but Terramorphic Expanse provides strictly more flexibility since it can find any basic.

Activating Myriad Landscape costs 2 mana and sacrifices the land, leaving KimiK2 Valley with only 4 lands (Island, Forest, Plains, and the two fetched basics) after resolution. With 5 mana available (Island, Myriad Landscape, Forest, Plains + the 2 from sacrificing), they could have cast Gwafa Hazid (1WU) or Windborn Muse (3W) this turn instead. More importantly, GLM47 Gramps is at 2 life with Katsumasa as a potential threat, and Gwafa Hazid could lock down Katsumasa or other threats. Myriad Landscape activation is fine long-term ramp, but sequencing matters - they should play the Gruul Turf or Terramorphic Expanse from hand first as their land drop, then decide whether to activate Myriad Landscape or cast a spell. Activating Myriad Landscape before making a land drop wastes the opportunity to play a land this turn alongside the activation.

With GLM47 Gramps at only 2 life, Windborn Muse would have been a strong defensive play - its flying body and attack tax ({2} per attacking creature) provides significant protection. Gwafa Hazid requires additional mana investment ({W}{U} + tap) to neutralize one creature at a time, and the controller draws a card as compensation. However, Gwafa does cost 1 less mana (3 vs 4), so casting him now when mana is tight is reasonable. The main concern is that Windborn Muse's passive protection is generally more impactful in a 4-player game where multiple opponents might attack, whereas Gwafa's activated ability is slow and card-disadvantageous.

Casting Sigarda, Heron's Grace (5 mana) before playing a Forest from hand. Gem3F Coach has two Forests in hand and should play a land first to have more mana available for future turns or to potentially cast additional spells. Additionally, casting Heronblade Elite first (3 mana) would allow it to get a +1/+1 counter when Sigarda enters (since Sigarda is a Human triggering Heronblade Elite, though Sigarda is an Angel not a Human - wait, Heronblade Elite triggers on 'another Human enters'). Actually, Sigarda is an Angel, not a Human, so Heronblade Elite wouldn't trigger. However, the sequencing concern about playing a land before casting spells remains valid. Also, with Dearly Departed in the graveyard, Human creatures enter with an additional +1/+1 counter - but Sigarda is an Angel, not Human. Heronblade Elite IS a Human though, and would enter with an extra counter from Dearly Departed, making it a 2/2 with vigilance and mana production equal to its power. Casting Heronblade Elite first (3 mana), it enters as a 2/2 due to Dearly Departed, then with remaining mana after playing a land (would have 7 mana total with land drop), could still cast Sigarda (5 mana) - but that's 8 mana total needed. With current lands (4 lands + Sol Ring + Eldrazi Spawn = 7 mana), playing a Forest would give 8 mana. So the better line would be: Play Forest, cast Heronblade Elite (3 mana, enters as 2/2 from Dearly Departed), then cast Sigarda (5 mana, Heronblade Elite triggers getting another counter becoming 3/3). This generates significantly more value.

message: Pick triggered ability (goes to the stack first)
annotation_description: GLM47 Gramps is at 2 life. Gem3F Coach has Abzan Falconer (2/3) and Ainok Bond-Kin (2/1) that can attack. Gramps only has Katsumasa (3/3 flying) and Silver Myr (1/1) as potential blockers. Attacking with both creatures forces Gramps to block both or die - they'd need to use both blockers to survive. Even attacking with just one 2-power creature forces Gramps to chump block or die.

GLM47 Gramps is at 2 life with only 2 potential blockers (Katsumasa the Animator 3/3 flying and Silver Myr 1/1). Attacking with 3+ creatures guarantees lethal since at least one attacker gets through unblocked for 2+ damage. Herald of War (flying), Ainok Bond-Kin, and Bastion Protector attacking would force Gramps to leave at least one unblocked.

Attacking with Gwafa Hazid, Profiteer is questionable because Gwafa is much more valuable as a tap ability creature (putting bribery counters on threats to prevent them from attacking or blocking) than as a 2/2 attacker. Tapping Gwafa to attack means he can't use his ability this turn cycle. With Coach having a growing board (Abzan Falconer, Ainok Bond-Kin with outlast synergies) and Johnny having Ravenous Baloth, Gwafa's bribery ability is very relevant for controlling threats. Additionally, attacking into opponents who could easily block a 2/2 for minimal damage isn't worth losing access to Gwafa's powerful tap ability.

Declined to cast Ruinous Intrusion on Howling Mine, which benefits opponents twice as much as Coach in a 3-player game. Exiling it would also put 2 +1/+1 counters on a creature, synergizing with Abzan Falconer (flying) and Ainok Bond-Kin (first strike).

Enduring Scalelord (4/4 flyer) would provide a much stronger immediate board presence and threat, and synergizes well with the +1/+1 counter theme (Abzan Falconer gives flying to creatures with counters, and Scalelord grows whenever counters are placed on other creatures). Heronblade Elite is a smaller creature that needs time and more Humans to become impactful.

message: Pick triggered ability (goes to the stack first)
annotation_description: With Sol Ring untapped providing 2 colorless mana and Dearly Departed in the graveyard, activating Sigarda's ability to create a 1/1 Human Soldier token would result in a 2/2 token (due to Dearly Departed's +1/+1 counter) that has both flying (Abzan Falconer) and first strike (Ainok Bond-Kin). This is significant free value from an activated ability at instant speed during combat.

Gem3F Coach appears to have not attacked when they had safe, profitable attacks available. Sigarda, Heron's Grace is a 4/5 flyer that could attack Qwen3L Johnny (40hp) with no flying blockers available. Additionally, other creatures could potentially attack. Even with Windborn Muse taxing attacks against KimiK2 Valley, attacking Johnny with flyers and ground creatures was free value.

Drumhunter (2/2) blocking Abzan Falconer (2/3) results in Drumhunter dying without killing the Falconer. Drumhunter is a value creature that provides card draw and mana, making this an unfavorable trade.

message: Select card to discard (selected 0 of 2, min 2)
annotation_description: At 12 life with only Ravenous Baloth as a creature, Behemoth Sledge's lifelink would be very valuable for survival. War Cadence and Terra Ravager are both situational and less impactful given the current board state and low life total.

Homeward Path only produces colorless mana and its activated ability isn't relevant right now - there are no steal effects threatening Valley's creatures. With all lands tapped and spells like Rites of Flourishing (2G), Humble Defector (1R), and Reverse the Sands (6WW) in hand, colored mana production is much more important.

KimiK2 Valley chose to attack Gem3F Coach (47hp) instead of Qwen3L Johnny (12hp). Johnny is at critically low life and has only a Ravenous Baloth as a blocker (no Windborn Muse tax to worry about). Windborn Muse is a 2/3 flyer, and Selfless Squire is at least 1/1 (possibly larger with counters). Attacking Johnny could apply lethal pressure or force them to sacrifice their Ravenous Baloth for life gain, weakening their board. Meanwhile, attacking Coach at 47hp with a 2/3 flyer barely dents their life total. However, Coach does have the stronger board position long-term, and Valley may want to keep Johnny alive as a buffer against Coach. The reasoning is debatable but attacking the 12hp player seems more impactful.

Equipping Swiftfoot Boots to Herald of War rather than Sigarda, Heron's Grace. Sigarda provides hexproof to the player and all Human creatures, making her the highest-value protection target. If Sigarda is removed, the entire team loses hexproof protection.

At 3 life, Johnny is in a desperate situation. They chose to activate Ravenous Baloth's sacrifice ability to gain 4 life (going to 7), but this sacrifices their only creature - a 4/4 Beast that serves as both a blocker and their only board presence. With Rampaging Baloths in hand costing {4}{G}{G} and only having access to 2 green sources (2 Forests) plus Sol Ring and Selesnya Guildgate, they can't cast it this turn. However, the decision presented is between activating Ravenous Baloth (sacrificing it) versus casting Rampaging Baloths. Since they can't cast Rampaging Baloths (insufficient green mana), sacrificing the Baloth for 4 life is understandable given their critical life total. But they should consider whether keeping the 4/4 blocker alive is more valuable than 4 life. With Gem3F Coach having tapped creatures and KimiK2 Valley having a Selfless Squire (which starts as 1/1 but could be larger), the 4/4 blocker could prevent more than 4 damage. Additionally, they have lands in hand (Boros Guildgate, Boros Garrison, Mountain, Homeward Path) they should play first. The real issue is sacrificing their only meaningful creature when they could play a land first and potentially set up for Rampaging Baloths next turn while keeping the Baloth as a blocker this turn cycle.

Discarded Boros Guildgate (which produces R or W) over Homeward Path (which only produces colorless), when the hand is full of red-intensive spells like Crater Hellion (4RR), Terra Ravager (2RR), and War Cadence (2R). Homeward Path's activated ability has minimal relevance in this game state.

Casting Tempt with Discovery when Qwen3L Johnny is at 6 life and could potentially be finished off soon. Tempt with Discovery lets each opponent search for a land too - giving the struggling Johnny free ramp to potentially stabilize, and giving Coach (who is at 47 life and the real threat) additional lands. With Rites of Flourishing also in hand, Valley is helping opponents ramp when the board state calls for closing out the game. Additionally, Valley has Reverse the Sands in hand which becomes more powerful the wider the life total gap is - helping opponents ramp makes it harder to maintain that advantage. That said, Valley does need lands themselves (only 7 lands with expensive cards in hand), so the ramp isn't without merit.

KimiK2 Valley cast Humble Defector (a 2/1 that gives an opponent card draw when activated) in the postcombat main phase when they had several other productive plays available. With 8 cards in hand including Rites of Flourishing (which would help ramp and draw), bounce lands (Gruul Turf, Selesnya Sanctuary), and Reverse the Sands (which could be game-winning given the life total disparity of 28 vs 6 vs 47), casting Humble Defector is low-impact. The Defector primarily benefits opponents - it gives them cards when activated and has a tiny 2/1 body. Meanwhile, Rites of Flourishing would accelerate Valley's game plan of playing multiple lands from hand and drawing extra cards, and could be cast with the available mana.

At 6 life with only 6 lands (5 untapped after playing Homeward Path), Johnny is in a desperate situation. Druidic Satchel costs 3 to cast and then 2 more to activate, meaning it won't generate value until next turn at the earliest. Meanwhile, Harmonize (costing 2GG) would draw 3 cards immediately, potentially finding answers or lands to stabilize. With Gem3F Coach at 47 life having creatures on board and KimiK2 Valley at 28 life with a Selfless Squire, Johnny needs to find answers fast. Druidic Satchel is a slow value engine that's terrible when you're at 6 life and need immediate impact. The Satchel's best case next turn is revealing a land (ramp) or creature (1/1 token) or gaining 2 life - none of which meaningfully stabilize at 6 life. Harmonize finding 3 cards gives much better odds of finding something impactful.
